segmentation.text: outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
any vehicle, whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
an unobstructed width of the highway
shall be left for the free passage of other vehicles
a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.

This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: st.highway: "the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders" (DEF-NRS-484A-095, "the entire width between the boundary lines of every way"); x is upon it where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies).

'stop', prohibited here, takes DEF-NRS-484A-260 ("any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device"); 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155, "the standing of a vehicle") and 'leave standing' (DEF-NRS-484A-250, "the halting of a vehicle") are halts too. The halt is drv.motion.halted ("speed ... at or below speed_floor ... with no minimum duration", kin.speed), which observes any halting, even momentary. The definition's exclusions are carried beside it: a halt behind another road user ahead in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the conflict standoff gap (rel.surface_gap) avoids a conflict; a halt while a police officer's stop direction (dev.human_direction, indication stop) or a signal showing a red indication or a stop sign (dev.traffic_signal, dev.stop_sign) governs (dev.governs) the travel region x occupies is in compliance with directions. Purposes of parking and standing (loading, passengers) are not observable and are read through the halt (observable_reading purpose).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed by id; 'whether attended or unattended' excludes no member.

The paved or main-traveled part of the highway is the st.roadway ("the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder"; DEF-NRS-484A-220, "that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder"); x halts upon it where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies). A paved shoulder is off it: the words set the main-traveled part against the part off it where the vehicle may be left. st.roadway is 'not a stand-in' for the sidewalk.

A vehicle disabled on the roadway so that stopping cannot be avoided is read through its nearest observables, the same as the earlier mapping of 'a disabled vehicle' in this iteration: its engine or motor not running, so that propulsion is unavailable (kin.engine_running: "the vehicle's engine or motor is running, so that propulsion is available", false), with its hazard lamps flashing (sig.hazard: "both indicators flashing together"), while it occupies the roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway). kin.engine_running is 'not a stand-in' for motion or a halt, and is not used as either; the gap records that the disability itself has no atom.

operationalizations.standard: practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway
operationalizations.convention: Off-road stopping convention: moving off the main-traveled part is practicable where a shoulder lies within the reach of a short lateral move from the halted vehicle's body; the ground distance from the body to the nearest shoulder is the measured magnitude compared with the reach.

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies inside a business district or a residence district declared for the map or the trace.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; at the observation x's footprint overlaps a st.highway (rel.occupies) and asm.within_business_or_residence_district does not hold; and x is not disabled there: not (kin.engine_running false and sig.hazard on while x occupies a st.roadway).
obligation: It is not the case that, at the observation, x is halted (drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution) with its footprint overlapping a st.roadway, while some st.shoulder lies within p.offroad_stop_reach of x's body (st.region_geometry distance), unless the halt falls under the exclusions of the defined 'stop': some other road user is ahead of x in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a surface gap (rel.surface_gap) at most p.stopping_conflict_gap, or a dev.human_direction with indication stop, a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.stop_sign governs (dev.governs) a travel region x occupies.

narrowings.why: 'stop, park or leave standing' are read through the halt itself; the purposes that set parking and standing apart (loading, receiving passengers) are not observable, and every halt is a stop under the definition that applies, so none is lost.
'practicable' is read through the distance to a shoulder only; the shoulder's width, surface and load-bearing are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.motor_vehicle) on a rural highway (asm.within_business_or_residence_district declared false) halts with its footprint on the st.roadway, engine running, no hazard lamps, nothing ahead and no device governing; a st.shoulder lies within p.offroad_stop_reach of its body.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x halts on the roadway of a rural bridge with no shoulder within p.offroad_stop_reach; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x halts on the roadway in a declared residence district (asm.within_business_or_residence_district true).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x halts on the rural roadway beside a mapped shoulder, but the source maps regions without their outline, so the distance to the shoulder is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x halts on the rural roadway with its engine not running and its hazard lamps flashing: the disabled-vehicle exception applies.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: x halts on the rural roadway behind a halted truck ahead in its lane at a surface gap below p.stopping_conflict_gap, a shoulder within reach: the halt avoids a conflict and is no prohibited stop.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the carla_scene_graph acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.offroad_stop_reach
param_proposals.convention: Off-road stopping reach: the ground distance from a halted vehicle's body to a shoulder within which moving off the main-traveled part counts as practicable; about one lane width of lateral movement.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book lane and shoulder widths

param_proposals.name: p.stopping_conflict_gap
param_proposals.convention: Conflict standoff: the largest surface gap from a halted road user's body to another road user ahead of it at which the halt counts as necessary to avoid a conflict; a queue spacing at standstill.
param_proposals.source: queue spacing at standstill (traffic-flow jam-density conventions)

gaps.proposal: `ru.disabled` | a vehicle that cannot proceed under its own power, by a mechanical failure, crash damage or a flat tyre, as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** a vehicle parked with its engine off, or one showing hazard lamps | general — decides whether moving the vehicle off the roadway can be carried out, which the disabled-vehicle exception turns on
